profile.headline: Engineer, educator, and researcher working where business, engineering, and AI meet
profile.bio: I spent years as a high-tech engineer in advanced manufacturing before moving into business education. Today I teach business analytics and research methods, lead student capstone projects, and research how AI is reshaping business and engineering practice. I believe the hardest and most interesting problems now sit between disciplines.
profile.bio2: This site is my working window into three areas: student experiential learning projects built on real business problems; AI Watch, a curated list of impactful AI videos, articles, and papers; and Diamond Market Watch, a biweekly tracker of natural and lab-grown diamond prices.
profile.statement: Built on real-world data and live business scenarios, these student projects train the judgment textbooks can’t, and several led to public presentations and showcases.

projects.title: Bringing Solar Light to the North San Joaquin Valley

numbers.name: Numbers
items: potential sites found by an AI platform

subs.title: LightScope campus siting map
subs.text: Night-time field survey of 5 University of the Pacific sites turned into an interactive siting map: 13 lighting zones, 28 assessed points (7 critical, 18 high-need), and 64 planned fixture locations.

subs.title: AI lead-intelligence platform
subs.text: Seven AI agents pull from six public data sources to find and rank sites that need solar lighting: 300+ potential sites identified and 100+ opportunities ranked across 13 market segments.

subs.title: Live market dashboard
subs.text: An e-commerce and residential dashboard built with SQL, Python, and Google Looker Studio, combining market research and competitor analysis to support pricing and targeting decisions.

subs.title: Solar bollard teardown and 3D model
subs.text: Reverse engineering of a commercial solar bollard: product teardown, bill of materials, CAD model, and manufacturing process analysis, the groundwork for a U.S.-made, BABA-compliant product.

subs.title: Market and supplier analysis
subs.text: Competitive landscape of 19 solar lighting suppliers, 8 Portor products catalogued, and a 32-bollard photometric layout for the campus from Portor Lighting.

subs.title: Investor pitch and video
subs.text: Investor pitch at Smart Living Silicon Valley 2026, an "Illuminating the Miracle Mile" pilot proposal for five downtown Stockton sites, and an AI-assisted "Invest in Stockton" manufacturing video.

subs.title: Workforce training framework
subs.text: A training framework for Solar Light Product Assembly Technicians, with a plan to turn it into a high school summer camp for local workforce development.

emerging needs and opportunities.name: Emerging needs and opportunities
items: Campuses, municipalities, and commercial sites are modernizing lighting on multi-year programs, which creates timing opportunities for broader adoption.
Small business owners want proof of payback before committing; consumer demand is large but price-sensitive.
Institutions value no-trench installation but want low-risk pilots first.
Pooled buyers such as HOAs and gated communities can meet supplier minimums that single homeowners cannot.
A BABA-compliant, U.S.-manufactured product opens doors to domestic manufacturing and public-sector buyers; it needs external funding and in-house engineering to move forward.

long-term vision.name: Long-term vision
items: New entity, pilot manufacturing facility, and BABA-compliant prototype
Manufacturing, sales, and service operations reach break-even
Fully operational manufacturer with protected IP, in-house design, manufacturing, and installation

student voices.name: Student voices
items: This was my chance to actually do the work: research, build a dashboard, and eventually sit across the table from executives and project managers, making the case for why this matters and how it can change sustainability in our community.

The project gave me a real environment where effort had consequences. I had to learn AI, build systems, assess sites at night, organize data, prepare proposals, speak with professionals, manage relationships, and continue even when the main result, a closed sale, had not happened yet.

One of the most valuable parts of this experience was working on a project with multiple stakeholders and open-ended engineering challenges. Unlike many classroom assignments, this project required collaboration, organization, and problem-solving throughout the entire process.

outcomes.name: Outcomes
items: 2 of the 3 student research assistants have already secured jobs.
Portor Lighting agreed to offer more internships, including commission-based sales internships for University of the Pacific students.
What began as installing a few bollards on campus grew into reusable digital tools (LightScope, the lead-intelligence platform, a 3D bollard model) and a regional framework for future projects.
Two written letters of support from University of the Pacific Public Safety, plus team visits to Portor Lighting's facility in Ontario, CA and the Port of Stockton.
The work opened doors to the Miracle Mile revitalization effort in Stockton and to district-level location research.

projects.funder: North Valley Thrive (THRIVE) Catalyst grant · Idea Stage
projects.summary: Funded by North Valley Thrive, this one-year project tested whether a lighting manufacturer could bring its solar lighting products, and eventually its manufacturing, to the North San Joaquin Valley. With industry partner Portor Lighting, three student research assistants surveyed campus sites at night, built a campus siting map and an AI lead-intelligence platform, reverse-engineered a solar bollard, pitched to investors, and confirmed a pathway to Buy America (BABA 2021) compliance. The project found real market and community interest and now moves to its next phase: seeking funding for a local manufacturing entity.
